article.intro: Below is information useful to size and execute a client engagement. Per-bullet, short answers are preferred. Note "n/a" or "not yet tracked" rather than skipping; the presence of an answer is signal, including "we don't track this."
section.00.title: Basics
req.00-01: Company name (legal entity + brand if different)
req.00-02: Engagement context: sell-side preparation, buy-side review, post-close value creation, or other
req.00-03: Annual recurring revenue (most recent quarter, plus prior 12 months if available)
req.00-04: If applicable, funding stage and most recent round details (date, lead investor, headline valuation)
req.00-05: Business model (B2B SaaS, B2C subscription, enterprise license + services, marketplace, other)
req.00-06: Geographies of operation (revenue presence; engineering presence if different)
req.00-07: Headquarters jurisdiction (incorporation entity + primary operating location)
req.00-08: Company age (founding year; note any major pivot)
req.00-10: Year-over-year growth rate (revenue, and headcount if a different signal)
section.01.title: Product
req.01-01: One-paragraph product description: what it does, who buys it, the problem it solves
req.01-02: Target market: primary buyer persona, segment (SMB / mid-market / enterprise), industry vertical(s)
req.01-03: Product roadmap snapshot: current-quarter priorities + next-12-month outlook
req.01-04: Top three features by adoption (DAU/MAU or equivalent engagement metric)
req.01-05: Customer profile: typical contract size, contract length, top concentration risk
req.01-06: Competitive landscape: three to five named alternatives and how the product differentiates
req.01-07: Operational scale: low (internal tools or small user base), moderate (thousands of users with steady growth), or high (millions of users or high transaction volume)
section.02.title: Software Architecture
req.02-01: High-level architecture diagram (PDF or image): logical components, data flow, external integrations
req.02-02: Technology stack: primary languages, frameworks, databases, infrastructure providers
req.02-03: Repository organization: monorepo vs. polyrepo, number of services, approximate lines of code
req.02-04: Engineering FTE count: total and breakdown by team (product engineering, infrastructure / SRE, security, data)
req.02-05: Product personnel cost: annual fully-loaded cost for product managers and designers, if tracked separately from engineering
req.02-06: Annual build and tooling cost: IDE licenses, CI/CD platform, observability tooling
req.02-07: Third-party dependency overview: major licensed libraries or APIs + renewal exposure
req.02-08: Most recent technical-debt assessment or code-quality report (SonarQube, CodeClimate, equivalent) if available
section.03.title: Infrastructure & Operations
req.03-01: Hosting model: cloud provider(s), self-hosted / managed mix, primary region(s)
req.03-02: The past three months' monthly hosting and infrastructure spend
req.03-03: 12–24 months of hosting and infrastructure spend history if available
req.03-04: Headcount dedicated to infrastructure operations (FTE equivalent)
req.03-05: Monitoring and alerting stack (tools, on-call rotation, escalation paths)
req.03-06: Deployment frequency to production (e.g., multiple/day, weekly, monthly, quarterly)
req.03-07: Capacity headroom: current utilization vs. provisioned
req.03-08: Material capital expenditure on infrastructure in the last 12 months
section.04.title: SDLC
req.04-01: Development methodology (Agile, Scrum, Kanban, Waterfall, hybrid) and release cadence
req.04-02: Branching strategy (trunk-based, Gitflow, feature-branch) and code-review process
req.04-03: Test coverage targets: unit / integration / end-to-end (measured percentage if tracked)
req.04-04: Production deployment process: manual or automated, gating criteria, rollback approach
req.04-05: Production incidents: quarterly counts over the last 24 months (or 12 if 24 unavailable), with severity distribution and mean time to resolution
req.04-06: Active maintenance burden as a percentage of engineering time
req.04-07: Annual investment planned for technical-debt remediation (headcount budgeted, capex allocated, or specific roadmap commitments — e.g., "rewriting the legacy billing system in 2027")
req.04-08: Open bugs by severity (P0 / P1 / P2 / P3) and aging
req.04-09: Engineering operating model: in-house, outsourced, hybrid (with rough split)
section.05.title: Data, Analytics & AI
req.05-01: Data architecture overview: primary data stores, pipelines, warehousing platform
req.05-02: Data sensitivity classification: customer PII, financial, health, or other regulated categories handled
req.05-03: ML/AI capabilities in production (if any): models, training infrastructure, monitoring
req.05-04: Third-party data dependencies: licensed datasets, model providers, API integrations
req.05-05: Analytics stack: BI tooling, internal dashboards, customer-facing reporting
section.06.title: Security
req.06-01: Most recent penetration test (date, executive summary if shareable, remediation status)
req.06-02: Security incident history: any reportable events in the last 24 months
req.06-03: Access controls: SSO/MFA coverage, privileged-access management approach
req.06-04: Compliance certifications maintained (SOC 2, ISO 27001, HITRUST, PCI DSS, others)
req.06-05: Business continuity and disaster recovery plan: RPO/RTO targets, last tested date
section.07.title: People & Organization
req.07-01: Organizational chart with reporting lines (executive team + engineering leadership)
req.07-02: Engineering headcount by role: ICs vs. managers, seniority distribution, contractor mix
req.07-03: Average fully-loaded engineering salary, or salary band by level
req.07-04: Key-person dependencies: single points of knowledge, succession plans
req.07-05: Attrition: voluntary and involuntary turnover in the last 24 months
req.07-06: Twelve-month hiring plan: net new headcount, key roles, expected start dates
req.07-07: Recent organizational transformation: re-orgs, leadership changes, methodology shifts in the last 24 months
section.08.title: Corporate IT
req.08-01: Enterprise applications inventory: ERP, CRM, HRIS, finance, communication tools
req.08-02: Identity and access management: SSO provider, directory service, provisioning workflow
req.08-03: Annual IT spend: software licensing, hardware, support services
section.09.title: Governance & Compliance
req.09-01: Data categories handled (PII, PHI, financial, regulated industry data)
req.09-02: Jurisdictions of operation: where customers reside, where data is stored, where employees work
req.09-03: Applicable regulatory frameworks (e.g., GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA, SOX, PCI DSS, NIS2, EU AI Act)
req.09-04: Audit history: outstanding remediation items from third-party audits
req.09-05: Data-processing agreements: standard contracts, cross-border transfer mechanisms (SCCs, DPAs)
xlsx.instructions:
Instructions

This spreadsheet is the structured response surface for the GST
Information Request List. Each section mirrors a Virtual Data Room
(VDR) folder; together they cover the inputs GST needs to size and
execute the engagement.

Column layout on the main sheet:
  A  Reference      short ID per request (e.g., "0-01"). Quote it
                   back in conversation or in your VDR.
  B  Request        the structured information GST is asking for.
  C  Status         OPEN, PARTIAL, or CLOSED. Pre-filled OPEN on
                   every row; update as you progress.
  D  File Location  OPTIONAL. The filename, VDR path, or share-link
                   where the corresponding artifact lives.
  E  Comments       OPTIONAL. More of the answer — anything that did
                   not fit in Response. Read as part of your answer.
  F  Notes          OPTIONAL. Caveats and context about the answer
                   (timing, confidentiality, who to ask).
  G  Response       your free-text answer.

All four of D, E, F and G are read into the deliverable GST builds
from this workbook. Response and Comments are combined into the
answer; File Location and Notes are carried alongside it as source
and caveat. None of it is a private side channel — if you would
not want it read back to you, leave it out.

Status workflow (column C):
  OPEN     no response yet. Cell color: white.
  PARTIAL  answer in progress or awaiting input. Cell auto-colors
           cream when value is set to PARTIAL.
  CLOSED   answered and complete. Cell auto-colors light green
           when value is set to CLOSED.

Click any Status cell to use the in-cell dropdown. Cell color
updates automatically as the value changes (no manual recolor).

1. Set Status (column C) to PARTIAL or CLOSED as you progress.
2. Fill answers in column G (Response) alongside each request in B.
3. If you are attaching a file or pointing to a VDR folder, put the
   reference in column D (File Location). D and G may be used together.
4. Use column E (Comments) when the answer runs past what fits in
   Response. It is read as a continuation of your answer, so put
   answers there — not remarks about the answer.
5. Use column F (Notes) for anything that is NOT an answer
   ("scheduled for Q3 refresh", "confidential, discuss in call").
6. Type "n/a" or "not yet tracked" rather than leaving a Response
   cell blank. The presence of an answer is signal, including
   "we do not track this."
7. Section header rows (e.g., "00 — BASICS") delimit the {sectionCount} request
   areas. Per-section context lives in the canonical GST Information
   Request List article.
xlsx.handbackWithTarget: Return the filled file to your Global Strategic Technologies engagement lead.
xlsx.handbackWithoutTarget: Return the filled file to your Global Strategic Technologies point of contact.
xlsx.statusError: Status must be OPEN, PARTIAL, or CLOSED.
